name: Besh-Tash National Park
near: Kojuchak — the village at the gorge entrance (Lonely Planet); Beshtash — ~12.9 km in a straight line from the catalogue point (OSM). The town of Talas is ~13 km north of the start of the park (central-asia.guide).
elev: From 1,100 to 3,500–3,600 m (too.kg — up to 3,500 m; central-asia.guide — up to 3,600 m); the main lake is at about 3,000 m.
short: A nature park in the Talas Ala-Too (established 1996) along the 30-km Besh-Tash Gorge: juniper and spruce forests, eight mountain lakes, rare animals and the turquoise Lake Besh-Tash at ~3,000 m.
desc: Besh-Tash State Nature Park was established in 1996 in the Talas Range mountains south of the town of Talas and covers the gorges of Besh-Tash, Kolba, Kumush-Tag and Urmaral (too.kg; nomad.kg). Elevations range from 1,100 to 3,500–3,600 m; the park has eight mountain lakes, the largest being Besh-Tash (~3,000 m, depth 28 m) (too.kg; central-asia.guide). Flora — more than 800 plant species, including Tian Shan spruce and the endemic Semenov's fir, juniper, sea buckthorn; fauna — snow leopard, Turkestan lynx, brown bear, golden eagle, bearded vulture, maral (Altai red deer) (about 100 marals were brought in 2022) (nomad.kg; map.kg; central-asia.guide). Hunting is prohibited, and poaching is monitored with camera traps (map.kg, 2024). The area differs between sources: 13,701 ha (central-asia.guide) and more than 30,000 ha (nomad.kg). The name means “five stones” — from a legend about robbers and five stones in the gorge (too.kg).
guide: Besh-Tash is the most accessible “real” mountain park in Talas: the gorge entrance is only 13 km from the town, and the road along the river valley runs almost 30 km to a turquoise lake at three thousand metres. Pay the fee at the checkpoint (250 som per person and 400 per car), then choose: in a passenger car — a picnic and a night by the river; in an SUV or on foot — to the lake. Look for Semenov's fir in the forest — an endemic found almost nowhere else — and keep an eye on the slopes: maral live in the park, and camera traps catch the tracks of snow leopards. In May–June the slopes are full of tulips; in September there is golden autumn and sea buckthorn.
see: The gorges of Besh-Tash, Kolba, Kumush-Tag and Urmaral; Lake Besh-Tash (~3,000 m) and the other of the eight mountain lakes; forests of Tian Shan spruce, Semenov's fir and juniper; the “five stones” in the gorge; tulips in bloom (May–June); sea buckthorn and golden autumn (September) (too.kg; nomad.kg).
skip: You've already been to Ala-Archa or the Karakol park and aren't planning an overnight stay — a day trip will give similar views. You have no SUV and no strength for 20–25 km on foot to the lake. You're looking for developed infrastructure — there is almost none here.
diff: Easy — walks and picnics in the lower part of the gorge by the checkpoint; medium — the hike to the lake (20–25 km one way) or the TUK loop trek; hard — multi-day treks (for example, the 9-day Explore-Share trek) (nomad.kg; tuk.kg).
when: May–June — tulips and blossoms; July–August — passes are open, it is warm, yurt camps operate; September — golden autumn, sea buckthorn; in winter access is limited and trails are under snow (nomad.kg).
hours: Entry is through the park checkpoint with payment of the fee; the checkpoint's opening hours are not published. In winter access is limited (nomad.kg).
daytime: Morning — for the drive to the lake and clear air; in the evening it gets cold quickly in the gorge (editorial).
how: From Talas south ~13 km to the gorge entrance at Kojuchak (central-asia.guide; Lonely Planet), then along a dirt road beside the Besh-Tash River to the checkpoint; from the checkpoint to the lake 20–25 km (nomad.kg). To Talas from Bishkek: GoBus via Kazakhstan (500 som, Kaktus 06.2025) or a marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi via Suusamyr and Otmok (~350 / from ~650 som). Your own car from Bishkek — about 4 h to the park (map.kg); fee for the Bishkek — Osh highway tunnels at the Sosnovka post: 50 som (Kyrgyz) / 200 som (foreign), since 01.01.2024.
needcar: Yes: a taxi or your own car from Talas to the checkpoint; inside the park — an SUV, on foot or on horseback (through CBT Talas).
self: Yes: no permit needed, only the fee at the checkpoint. For long routes and horse treks a CBT Talas guide is better; there is no mobile coverage in the upper part of the gorge.
roadtype: Paved road Talas — Kojuchak; then a dirt road along the gorge: to the checkpoint — passenger cars, further on — an SUV (nomad.kg).
traveltime: Bishkek — park ~4 h by car (map.kg, 2024; by public transport to Talas 5.5–8 h); Talas — gorge entrance ~20–30 min (estimate, 13 km).
stay: Equipped camping zones at different elevations, campfires allowed (map.kg, 2024); in summer — yurt camps in the gorge (nomad.kg; names and prices not found); at the lake — tents. Guesthouses — in Talas ($10–30, kyrgyzstan-tourism.com) and through CBT Talas.
net: There is no mobile coverage at the lake or in the upper part of the gorge (too.kg); in the lower part at Kojuchak — not confirmed.
entry: 250 som per person and 400 som per car (nomad.kg; publication year not given). At the entrance there is a gate where the fee is paid (central-asia.guide).
transfer: Not confirmed: a taxi/SUV from Talas — by arrangement. To Talas: GoBus 500 som (2025), marshrutka ~350 som, shared taxi from ~650 som.
bring: Cash for the fee (250 som/person + 400 som/car), a tent and warm clothes if staying overnight, water purification, repellent, trekking shoes; food — there are no shops inside the park.
warn: A protected area: hunting is prohibited, camera traps are in operation (map.kg). Brown bears live in the park — store your food properly. No mobile coverage in the upper part. Without an SUV, the lake is reachable only on foot, 20–25 km. In winter access is limited (snow).
food: Kumys and home cooking at the yurt camps in summer (not confirmed for specific places); sea buckthorn in September (nomad.kg); in Talas — dishes with Talas beans.
reviews: Google Maps: 5.0 from 7 ratings (listed as “Besh-Tash State Nature National Park”, catalogue check 10.2026). No large sample of reviews was found on TripAdvisor/2GIS.
p.sum: Besh-Tash National Park begins ~13 km south of Talas at the village of Kojuchak: at the entrance there is an automated checkpoint (since 28.07.2026; 250 som/person and 400 som/car according to the latest data), then a dirt road along the river with camping zones and summer yurts. A passenger car is enough for a picnic and a walk in the lower gorge, but for the upper meadows and the lake you need a 4×4. Stay overnight in Talas or in a tent; look for guides and horses through CBT Talas.

p.permits: No permit needed. Fee 250 som/person + 400 som/car (year not given); automated checkpoint since 28.07.2026 — payment by card/QR/e-wallet. For reference: the general rates of Kyrgyzstan's nature parks in 2025 — 150–700 som depending on category (Kyrgyz/CIS/foreigners).
p.access: The lower meadows by the river are accessible by car — suitable for families with children and older people for a picnic. Wheelchair — only on flat meadows. With a dog — be careful (wild animals).
